# hi

> hi is a single-binary CLI for hi5 machines and projects: it rents remote GPUs
> (Google Colab, Hugging Face Jobs, RunPod, Shadeform) with `hi compute`, starts
> projects from templates with `hi init`, sets up Ubuntu workstations with
> `hi install`, turns plain-words requests into shell commands with `hi q`,
> downloads your team's private Hugging Face data through a hi server with
> `hi data`, and puts a local service on a temporary public address with
> `hi net expose`. These notes are for coding agents such as Codex and Claude Code.

## Instructions for agents

1. Check whether hi is installed: `hi version`. If it is not, install the CLI
   only (no sudo, no system changes) with
   `curl -fsSL https://hi5.sh/install.sh | sh`; the binary lands in
   `~/.local/bin/hi`.
2. Load the hi skill, which matches the installed version and holds the rules
   you must follow. Print it with `hi skill --print`. To keep it for later
   sessions, ask the user before running `hi skill add hi --global` (every
   project) or `hi skill add hi` (this folder only).
3. Follow the skill rather than this page. The short version of its rules:
   ask before starting paid hardware and show the `--dry-run` plan first;
   always set `--max`; stop what you start and check `hi compute ls`; pass
   credentials with `--secret`, never `--env`; never approve your own requests
   on a hi server; and ask before `hi install`, `hi adduser`, `hi net`, or
   `hi update`, which change the machine. Get your team's data with `hi data`,
   never with a Hugging Face token of your own. Ask before `hi net expose`,
   keep its password, never use `--public` without the user's yes, and stop
   it when done.
4. Run `hi help`, `hi compute help`, or `hi init --help` for the exact options.

## Guide

- [Your first remote GPU](https://hi5.sh/guide/quickstart/): sign in, run a script, stop it
- [Let your coding agent use a GPU](https://hi5.sh/guide/tutorials/agent/): what to ask an agent, and what it does
- [Skills](https://hi5.sh/guide/reference/skill/): `hi skill` finds, installs, and updates agent skills from skills.sh, and writes the hi skill
- [All commands](https://hi5.sh/guide/reference/commands/): every command and option
- [Hand tasks to agents](https://hi5.sh/guide/agent/): `hi agent`, Claude Code, Codex, or Hermes on a task in a box, without permission prompts, with one report for every agent, and `--bundle web,office,data` for skills and the tools they need; `hi agent best-of` runs one task in several boxes, checks each, and ranks them, or with `--score` runs rounds that commit only gains, and `--then "<command>"` runs a command when they end
- [Review a whole repository](https://hi5.sh/guide/agent/review/): `hi agent review` has agents read a repository for security and correctness problems (also performance and maintainability), each in a locked box on a snapshot, here or fetched from a URL; hi checks every quoted line against the snapshot, a different agent confirms or rejects each finding, and `report.md` is recommendations that say what each finding assumes; `--since`, `--compare`, briefs of your own as areas, `--sarif`, and `show --html`; nothing is changed
- [Agent teams](https://hi5.sh/guide/team/) ([set up](https://hi5.sh/guide/team/setup/), [how it works](https://hi5.sh/guide/team/how-it-works/), [the app](https://hi5.sh/guide/team/app/), [help and chat](https://hi5.sh/guide/team/helper/), [keys](https://hi5.sh/guide/team/keys/), [dev and production](https://hi5.sh/guide/team/releases/), [deep reviews](https://hi5.sh/guide/team/reviews/), [folder and backups](https://hi5.sh/guide/team/folder/)): `hi team`, a virtual team of agents in one Slack channel: a Hermes lead talks with the people in plain language and keeps the specs, a coder and a reviewer work in boxes, and the lead merges what the reviewer approves; before a risky release the lead offers a deep review of the whole project (`hi team review --project`), which only an owner's yes to a named budget starts; `hi team key <name> openrouter` and `hi team env <name> KEY=VALUE` give the team its own OpenRouter key and the app its settings, and the app calls models at `$OPENROUTER_BASE_URL` without holding a key; `hi team snapshot`, `snapshots`, `restore`, and `backups` keep the lead's memory, the team's record, and the app's data (`$HI_DATA_DIR`) in restic snapshots, daily and before every release, optionally copied to an S3 bucket
- [Run code in a box](https://hi5.sh/guide/box/): `hi box`, a shell or a command in a rootless container with no credentials and a limited network, set up per project in `devcontainer.json` (`customizations.hi`, including `bundles`)
- [Share a local service](https://hi5.sh/guide/workstation/expose/): `hi net expose <port>`, a temporary public address for a service on this machine; ask the user first
- [Download your team's data](https://hi5.sh/guide/data/): `hi data`, your team's private Hugging Face datasets, models, and buckets through the hi server, on laptops, in boxes, in cloud jobs (`hi compute run --data`), and on machines you SSH into (`hi compute up --data`)
- [Ask for a command](https://hi5.sh/guide/q/): `hi q`, for people at a terminal; agents don't need it
- [Start a project](https://hi5.sh/guide/projects/): `hi init` templates, `--update`, and `--adopt`
- [Troubleshooting](https://hi5.sh/guide/reference/troubleshooting/): messages and what to do

## Optional

- [Install hi](https://hi5.sh/guide/install/): installer options and updating
- [Managed compute for your team](https://hi5.sh/guide/compute/managed/): requests and approvals through a hi server
- [Source](https://github.com/hi5sh/hi)
